what: attacker-side timing fingerprint — ROC-AUC over measured timing classes
method: windows of k consecutive observed latencies; features mean/std/min/max; logistic regression 50/50 split; held-out AUC with seeded bootstrap CI; single-gap threshold AUC and KS test per arm

real_gaps.note: inter-command gaps = attacker think time + server response (UPPER bound on traditional response latency); the fingerprinting target is the session timing ENVELOPE

fastpath_deterministic.note: real AdaptiveDeceiver template path timed in-process (no gateway)

gates.gate_basis: primary = directional single-gap AUC vs the real-vs-real control floor; windowed AUC reported as secondary (under-powered at this n)

reading: Unmitigated RAGIN serving is timing-fingerprintable: single-gap directional AUC 0.9834 vs a real-vs-real drift floor of 0.6759. Serving everything from the sub-ms fastpath is EQUALLY detectable (too fast; AUC 1.0) — mitigation must shape timing, not merely maximize fast-path coverage. Padding the deterministic path into the real envelope brings the arm to AUC 0.5512, at or below the drift floor — indistinguishable from a traditional honeypot by this channel. LLM latency cannot be padded down, so the deployed mitigation is: raise deterministic-path coverage and add an additive delay drawn from the measured real envelope.
limitations: real class uses inter-command gaps (think+response), not pure response latency — unobservable from logs; claims are about the timing envelope
real class is small (38 gaps, 13 sessions) — the drift-floor control is correspondingly coarse; field-deployment captures (RQ4) will tighten it
padded arm models additive sleep analytically (target drawn from the real envelope); a deployed system would sleep the remainder in-process
fastpath timings are in-process (no network stack); network jitter would narrow but not close the 3-orders-of-magnitude gap to LLM serves
windowed AUC is under-powered at this n (wide bootstrap CIs); the single-gap directional AUC with the control floor is the primary gate
